title: Groovy Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: println prints a value with a newline.

entries.name: Name a value
entries.summary: def declares a variable without spelling its type.
notes: Use numbers rather than quoted text for addition.

entries.name: Build a message
entries.summary: Double-quoted strings can place a variable in the text with a dollar sign.
notes: Single-quoted strings do not expand variables.

entries.name: Choose an action
entries.summary: if selects a block based on a rule.

example.code:
def score = 8
if (score >= 5) { println "Pass" } else { println "Try again" }

notes: Use a clear comparison when testing a score.

entries.name: Read a list item
entries.summary: A list stores ordered values. Its first position is zero.

entries.name: Read a named field
entries.summary: A map pairs keys with values. Dot syntax can read a simple text key.

example.code:
def book = [title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24]
println book.title

notes: A missing map value may be null; plan for that.

entries.name: Count across a range
entries.summary: The range 1..3 includes both endpoints. each visits the values.
notes: The ..< range leaves out its last endpoint.

entries.name: Name a small function
entries.summary: A closure is a block of reusable code. The arrow separates inputs from steps.

example.code:
def twice = { n -> n * 2 }
println twice(4)

notes: The last expression is the closure result.

entries.name: Transform each item
entries.summary: collect builds a list from a closure result for each item.
notes: it names the input when you omit an explicit closure input.

entries.name: Keep matching items
entries.summary: findAll keeps items for which the closure result is true.
notes: find reads one item, while findAll reads all matching items.

entries.name: Handle a missing object
entries.summary: ?. skips a property read on null. The Elvis operator ?: supplies a fallback for a false-like value.
notes: Elvis uses Groovy truth, so it can replace empty strings and zero too.

entries.name: Create an object
entries.summary: A class groups data fields and actions. Groovy supports named property values during construction.
notes: Spell property names exactly in the named arguments.
